added.d: Gangnam B-Side is a dark crime-mystery with grounded stakes and a serious tone, so it should fit his preference for pressure, justice, and moral weight better than flashy or comedic crime shows. It likely has enough violence and plot momentum to work, but because it is closer to a stylized crime revenge thriller than a courtroom/procedural drama, it is less exact than his top-loved titles and somewhat nearer to Taxi Driver in structure and energy.

This is a serious, grounded justice story with believable pressure, moral weight, and an oppressive-system conflict that matches what he rewards most. It should feel far closer to his loved, sincere shows than to the exaggerated, cartoonish style of Taxi Driver or Vincenzo; the only real mismatch is that it is a feature film, not a short series.

This is a grounded legal-crime mystery with sincere stakes, family pressure, and a clear justice goal, so it matches his preference for believable conflict and moral payoff. It also resembles his liked courtroom and case-driven shows more than the exaggerated action of his dropped titles, though as a feature film the format is only a partial fit.

This is a serious, grounded investigation drama with political tension, moral weight, and conflicting testimonies, so it aligns well with his preference for restrained, believable pressure over flashy spectacle. As a feature film it only gets a partial format fit, but its sober tone and case-driven structure resemble the more realistic, serious side of Undercover more than his dropped, exaggerated shows.

This is a grounded political-crime power struggle with believable motives, corruption, and pressure, so it fits his preference for serious, realistic stakes and moral tension. It also has strong legal/prosecutorial energy and no obvious comedy or spectacle problem; the only format mismatch is that it is a feature film, so the format score is capped.

This is a serious, grounded crime-drama with strong emotional pressure, moral weight, and a justice-driven core, so it fits his strongest preferences well. It is a feature film rather than a short recent series, so format is only a partial fit, but its restrained tone and sincere stakes are much closer to his loved shows than to the exaggerated shows he dropped.

It has a serious, grounded cat-and-mouse structure with real pressure, sacrifice, and political stakes, so it fits his preference for tense justice-and-mission stories more than stylized action. It is less case-by-case and less morally explicit than his favorite courtroom and revenge shows, and as a feature film it only gets a partial format fit.

This is a grounded, serious crime thriller with believable pressure, moral weight, and a bleak procedural drive, which matches his preference for realism and justice-focused tension. It resembles his loved investigative and justice stories more than his rejected stylized action shows, though as a feature film it is only a partial format fit for his series preference.

This looks grounded, serious, and emotionally heavy, with a real-mystery setup, parental grief, and investigative pressure rather than flashy spectacle. It should fit his preference for crime/drama with moral weight and restrained tone, though as a feature film it is only a partial format fit compared with his favored short series.

This is a serious, revenge-driven drama with strong emotional weight, moral pressure, and a grounded enough chain of cause and consequence, so it fits his realism bar much better than flashy or cartoonish action titles. It resembles As You Stood By in its dark justice/retribution focus, though as a feature film it gets the usual format limit and has less of the procedural casework he especially loves.

This is a serious, grounded espionage drama with believable pressure, moral stakes, and no cartoonish spectacle, so it should land much closer to Undercover than to his dropped over-the-top action shows. It also has the kind of tense, justice-adjacent, politically charged plotting he likes, though as a feature film it is only a partial format fit for his preference for concise series.
